title: Carly's dashboard: choose the layout
question: Same GymShift style as the cleaner home. Three ways to put 'what needs me' first. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Review Queue
options.lineage: One-at-a-time review, like a banking app's 'approve payment' screen
options.thesis: Carly works through what needs her one item at a time: one card, its facts, two clear buttons, then the next.
options.viewport: Top bar; 'Needs you · 1 of 7'; one large card (Maria Santos, extra 20 min, reason, tonight's shift, Approve / Decline); a 'next up' peek; Today's shifts as a compact pass below. On desktop the queue sits left, Today right.
options.risk: Fast for approvals, slower to scan everything at once; needs a 'see all' list too.

options.label: One List, Filters
options.thesis: Everything that needs Carly in one list, oldest first; chips with counts filter by Requests, Flags or Supplies.
options.viewport: Top bar; 'Needs you'; chips All 7 · Requests 2 · Flags 4 · Supplies 1; rows with an icon disc, who, what, when, and inline Approve/Decline on requests; Today's shifts and Export hours below. On desktop the list widens with a detail pane.
options.risk: A long mixed list can feel like email; it relies on clear icons and wording per type.

options.label: Grouped Sections
options.thesis: Three short sections in a fixed order: Requests to decide, Flags to check, Supplies to buy. Each says how many and stays scannable.
options.viewport: Top bar; 'Hi Carly · 7 things need you'; Requests (2) with inline Approve/Decline; Flags (4) as rows that open the detail; Supplies (1) with Done; Today and Export hours at the bottom. On desktop sections become columns.
options.risk: The most familiar of the three; sections with zero items must collapse cleanly.
